JLL is recognized for transforming facility management through an integrated Workplace Management platform, digital innovation, and sector-focused execution that strengthens operational resilience and business performance.

SAN ANTONIO, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As facility management continues to evolve from a largely operational function into a strategic contributor to workplace performance and enterprise resilience, JLL is demonstrating how an integrated approach can create measurable value for organizations across complex environments. Frost & Sullivan recognizes JLL with the 2026 North American Competitive Strategy Leadership Recognition in Facility Management for its ability to combine strategic transformation, digital capabilities, and sector expertise to strengthen its competitive position and deliver integrated facility management (IFM) solutions across the region.

Frost & Sullivan evaluates companies through a rigorous benchmarking process across two core dimensions: strategy effectiveness and strategy execution. JLL excelled in both, demonstrating its ability to align strategic initiatives with evolving market demands while executing them with consistency, scale, and measurable impact. "JLL is a recognized leader in IFM and workplace solutions across North America. Its competitive position is built on a clear strategic progression: redefining Facility Management through the Workplace Management platform, aligning its operating structure to support integrated delivery, and scaling digital and sector-specific capabilities across the United States and Canada. This approach enables JLL to serve commercial office, financial services, life sciences, technology, industrial and advanced manufacturing, data centers, healthcare, and government clients while linking facility operations more directly to business performance," said Janice Wung, Industry Principal, Homes & Buildings, Frost & Sullivan.

JLL's strategic approach centers on its Workplace Management platform, which brings together facilities management, technical services, sustainable operations, safety, sourcing and procurement, workplace experience, and technology-enabled delivery under a single operating structure. The platform supports greater standardization, governance, and scalability across multi-site portfolios while maintaining flexibility for sector-specific requirements.

Digital innovation further differentiates JLL's approach to facility management. Technologies, including Corrigo, JLL Smart Building Platform, Azara, and JLL Falcon AI, support work order and asset management, predictive maintenance, energy optimization, workplace analytics, and portfolio-level performance visibility. These capabilities enable clients to move beyond reactive facility operations toward more proactive, data-driven decision-making.

"We are honored Frost & Sullivan is recognizing JLL's work in facilities management," said Chris Fernandez, Americas Head of Workplace Management at JLL. "At its core, facilities management is about creating environments where people can do their best work while ensuring the buildings they depend on operate safely, reliably and efficiently every day. FM has evolved far beyond maintaining physical assets. Today, it sits at the intersection of workplace experience, operational resilience and business performance. This award reflects the dedication of our teams across North America who help clients care for both their buildings and the people inside them, ensuring workplaces support productivity, collaboration and long-term success."

Frost & Sullivan's recognition comes while broader changes are underway across the facility management industry. JLL's recent Global State of Facilities Management Report 2026 reveals that half of occupiers already view FM as a significant source of competitive advantage, with that figure projected to rise to more than four in five organizations by 2030. Meanwhile, 45% of occupiers are scaling AI across FM operations while nearly 70% have experienced disruptions from skilled labor shortages and technical skills gaps. These converging trends are accelerating demand for integrated workplace management strategies that combine operational expertise, technology and workforce capabilities to support business performance and resilience.

JLL has also demonstrated its ability to translate strategy into execution across complex, high-value environments. In 2025, the company secured integrated facilities management for WestJet's 1.9 million-square-foot portfolio spanning its headquarters and 17 Canadian airport locations, along with the facility maintenance and operations mandate for the $9.5 billion JFK New Terminal One project. For a global tech manufacturer, JLL moved the company's U.S. portfolio from reactive repairs to proactive IFM, saving nearly $1 million on HVAC costs in its first eight months and achieving 4% overall savings in the first year. JLL has also partnered with a Fortune 100 semiconductor company to build a digital FM strategy aimed at cost savings and operational excellence. Together, these engagements show JLL's ability to scale integrated facility management across demanding environments where reliability, compliance, operational resilience, and risk management are critical.

The company's competitive position is further strengthened by integrating energy management, decarbonization initiatives, ESG reporting, workplace experience, and space-utilization analysis into its FM delivery model, JLL addresses the increasingly interconnected priorities of corporate real estate, sustainability, HR, and business leaders.

Frost & Sullivan commends JLL for establishing a differentiated approach to facility management that connects operational performance with broader business outcomes. Through its combination of proprietary technology, advisory-led delivery, sector expertise, and customer-focused execution, JLL is helping shape the future of FM across North America.

Each year, Frost & Sullivan presents the Competitive Strategy Leadership recognition to a company that demonstrates outstanding strategy development and implementation, resulting in measurable improvements in market share, customer satisfaction, and competitive positioning. The recognition highlights forward-thinking organizations that are reshaping their industries through innovation and growth excellence.

Frost & Sullivan Best Practices Recognition

Frost & Sullivan's Best Practices Recognitions honor companies across regional and global markets that exhibit exceptional achievement and consistent excellence in areas such as leadership, technological innovation, customer experience, and strategic product development. Each recognition is the result of a rigorous analytical process in which Frost & Sullivan industry experts benchmark performance through comprehensive interviews, deep-dive analysis, and extensive secondary research. The goal is to identify true best-in-class organizations that are driving transformative growth and setting new industry standards.

MUMBAI, India & KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Clean energy solutions company Gentari and leading global investment firm KKR today announced that capital accounts advised by KKR have made a minority investment in Gentari Renewables India Pte Ltd, which holds Gentari’s renewables platform in India. ​​The investment will provide growth capital to support the platform’s continued expansion in the country.

India remains a key market for Gentari, underpinned by increasing renewable energy demand, supportive market fundamentals and long-term opportunities. The investment marks an important milestone in the evolution of Gentari’s renewables platform in the country. Today, Gentari's India platform has approximately 8 GW of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable energy capacity, with a robust development pipeline. The platform serves commercial and industrial customers, as well as government entities, through a diversified portfolio spanning solar, wind, hybrid and battery energy storage solutions, helping meet India’s growing clean energy needs. This reflects Gentari’s progress in scaling the business into one of its largest growth platforms. The strategic partnership with KKR brings together Gentari's development, execution and operating capabilities with KKR’s long-term investment and deep infrastructure experience to support the platform’s next phase of growth.

Sushil Purohit, Group Chief Executive Officer, Gentari, commented, "This strategic partnership reflects confidence in the scale and maturity of the platform we have built in India as well as the strength of our growth trajectory. We are pleased to welcome KKR as an investor, given its long-term investment approach and deep experience supporting infrastructure and energy businesses globally. With KKR’s support, we are well-positioned to continue scaling the business as a self-sustaining renewable energy platform focused on long-term value creation."

Hardik Shah, Partner, Asia Pacific Infrastructure, KKR, said, “India’s demand for reliable power is growing rapidly, creating a significant need for continued investment in the country’s energy infrastructure. We believe scaled platforms that can deliver increasingly sophisticated renewable energy solutions will have an important role to play in meeting that demand. Gentari has built strong capabilities across renewable generation, hybrid solutions and energy storage and we look forward to supporting the business in its next phase of growth.”

KKR has been investing in India’s infrastructure sector for more than a decade, with a focus on building and scaling platforms across sectors including renewable energy, power transmission, roads, logistics and transportation. In renewable energy, KKR has invested in Serentica Renewables and Hero Future Energies, building on KKR’s broader approach of supporting and scaling infrastructure platforms in India. Since 2011, KKR’s infrastructure platform has committed more than US$27 billion in energy transition and renewables infrastructure globally.

Following the investment, Gentari will continue to retain strategic oversight and operational control of the platform in India. This milestone reinforces Gentari's long-term commitment to India and supports the next phase of expansion of its renewables platform in the country.

About Gentari

As part of the PETRONAS Group, Gentari is a clean energy solutions company operating across Renewable Energy, Hydrogen and Green Mobility. Through these businesses, Gentari supports customers in addressing evolving energy needs while balancing energy security, reliability, and affordability. With 9.1 GW of renewable energy capacity installed and under construction globally, Gentari has established a growing presence across key markets including Malaysia, India and Australia. Its renewable energy portfolio spans solar, onshore and offshore wind, and battery energy storage, while its hydrogen and green mobility businesses continue to expand. Gentari is also advancing cross-border energy initiatives, including renewable electricity interconnection opportunities in Southeast Asia. By combining expertise across its businesses, Gentari helps customers optimise energy systems, strengthen operational resilience, and create long-term value. Gentari aims to be Asia Pacific's most valued clean energy solutions partner. For additional information, visit www.gentari.com.

KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. SINGAPORE, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JOYY Inc. (NASDAQ: JOYY) ("JOYY" or the "Company"), a leading global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

In the third quarter, JOYY maintained solid growth momentum. Total revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Social entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, up 8.8% year over year. BIGO Ads, including both first-party and third-party businesses, generated US$145.7 million in revenue, up 39.6% year over year, with its third-party advertising business sustaining strong growth of 52.3% year over year. SHOPLINE revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year. The contribution from non-livestreaming revenue further increased to 32.8% of total revenues this quarter, driven by the Company's multi-engine growth strategy.

JOYY's non-GAAP operating income reached US$46.6 million, up 14.6% year over year. Non-GAAP EBITDA reached US$55.7 million, up 10.1% year over year. Operating cash inflow for the quarter was US$102.2 million. As of September 30, 2026, JOYY held US$2.94 billion in net cash. Supported by the Company's strong cash flow generation and solid financial position, it continued to return capital to its shareholders for their long-term support through cash dividends and share repurchases. As of November 13, the Company has returned a total of US$536.0 million to shareholders this year.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY, commented, "We have continued to execute our multi-engine growth strategy, strengthening our core Social Entertainment business while developing Ad Tech and Smart Commerce as two new growth engines. Following our investments and business model validation over the past few years, the results of this strategy are becoming increasingly evident in sustained topline expansion. Looking ahead to 2027, we believe JOYY will enter an important phase as we advance our multi-engine growth strategy and translate our progress into stronger operating results. With increasingly clear growth paths across our three businesses, we are confident in the Company's ability to sustain solid revenue growth in 2027. We also expect greater scale, a stronger earnings mix, and improved operating efficiency to drive further growth in operating profitability." 

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - Social Entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, representing an increase of 8.8% from US$405.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - BIGO Ads revenue was US$145.7 million, representing an increase of 39.6% from US$104.4 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.
    - SHOPLINE revenue was US$37.8 million, representing an increase of 24.7% from US$30.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million.
  • Non-GAAP1 operating income was US$46.6 million, representing an increase of 14.6% from US$40.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP1 EBITDA was US$55.7 million, representing an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net cash as of September 30, 2026 was US$2940.5 million.
  • Net cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Social Entertainment Business

In the third quarter, Social Entertainment continued to deliver steady growth, with year-over-year growth momentum further accelerating. The Company's global average mobile MAUs reached 278.8 million, up 4.7% year over year. Livestreaming revenue reached US$419.8 million, up 8.1% year over year and 4.3% quarter over quarter. Driven by effective and refined operations, the number of core livestreaming paying users grew 8.1% year over year and 4.8% quarter over quarter.

Bigo Live, the Company's flagship product, continued its steady revenue growth, supported by ongoing improvements in content operations, its streamer ecosystem, and AI applications. In content operations, Bigo Live continued to build on its strengths as a global social platform to better cater to users' cross-regional content consumption and social interaction needs. Bigo Live further refined its cross-regional content distribution algorithms, expanded live translation coverage, and enhanced speech recognition in complex acoustic environments, making it easier for cross-language communication. These improvements drove continued growth in cross-regional gifting among users in developed markets. In terms of the streamer ecosystem, Bigo Live continued to invest in its community by refining growth and incentive mechanisms for new streamers. In particular, Bigo Live improved onboarding and guidance to help newly signed streamers successfully launch their first livestreams. These efforts contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream compared with the previous quarter, bolstering Bigo Live's high-quality content pipeline. Bigo Live continued to integrate AI into livestream interactions and virtual gifting, expanding its AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts to create a more personalized experience for users. In September, the share of total virtual gift consumption attributable to AI-generated interactive virtual gifts increased further to 35.4%.

Furthermore, Bigo Live continued to deepen local community engagement and foster vibrant creator ecosystems. In the Middle East and North Africa, as an official content partner of the 2026 Esports World Cup, Bigo Live delivered an immersive viewing format that integrated tournament livestreams with interactive experiences. Across Southeast Asia, Bigo Live hosted multiple mid-year galas in local markets, supporting the growth of local creators and the sustainable development of its ecosystem. In North America, BIGO Academy combined online growth challenges with offline recognition, highlighting the vitality of its creator ecosystem and strong user engagement. In South America, Bigo Live held its inaugural offline event in Brazil and organized roadshows in Colombia and Peru, expanding public awareness of the platform and fostering a more vibrant and inclusive local creator ecosystem.

BIGO Ads Advertising Technology Business

In the third quarter, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global traffic network, diversify its advertiser verticals and demand mix, while improving its algorithms and ad delivery efficiency. As a result, BIGO Ads' revenue reached US$145.7 million, up 39.6% year over year and 9.0% quarter over quarter. Its third-party advertising business, BIGO Audience Network, grew 52.3% year over year and 9.2% quarter over quarter.

On the supply side, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global developer ecosystem and broaden the high-quality traffic coverage. In the third quarter, SDK traffic grew 55.6% year over year. In October, BIGO Ads SDK became generally available via Google AdMob™ Mediation as an in-app bidding partner. Developers can now seamlessly access the BIGO Ads SDK through Google AdMob Mediation and tap into massive demand from global premium advertisers. This integration creates new opportunities for BIGO Ads to expand its premium traffic supply and reach a broader range of app categories.

On the demand side, BIGO Ads continued to strengthen its presence in key verticals by expanding its local advertiser base and accumulating more advertiser conversion data. These insights helped further refine its algorithms and optimize ad delivery solutions across different web-based verticals. Web-based advertising demand continued to accelerate, growing by approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, becoming a key driver of BIGO Ads' growth this quarter. Meanwhile, in-app demand maintained healthy growth momentum.

On the technology side, BIGO Ads continued to enhance its data and AI-driven algorithm capabilities to improve the precision and efficiency of ad delivery. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, the platform further upgraded its model architecture to support multiple conversion objectives and types of traffic, improving algorithm accuracy and iteration efficiency. Meanwhile, BIGO Ads continued to refine its bidding strategies to better assess the value of each ad impression and match advertiser budgets with available inventory more effectively. These improvements helped advertisers meet their ROI targets while enhancing the efficiency of BIGO Ads' traffic acquisition and monetization.

SHOPLINE E-Commerce Business

In the third quarter, SHOPLINE continued to focus on acquiring high-quality brand merchants, strengthening its presence in key markets, and enhancing its omnichannel commerce infrastructure and value-added services. SHOPLINE's revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter.

In the cross-border business, SHOPLINE enhanced its service offerings and local support to help these merchants migrate to its platform, manage operations across markets, and process cross-border transactions more efficiently. In the third quarter, revenue from cross-border merchants maintained strong momentum, growing 77.8% year over year. To support the growing base of brand merchants, the Company continued to enhance SHOPLINE Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management. These enhancements helped merchants manage cross-border payments easily and efficiently.

In AI Commerce, SHOPLINE's strategy revolves around helping merchants capture demand from AI channels and improve their operational efficiency. As AI agents change how consumers discover and purchase products, SHOPLINE continued to strengthen its capabilities and expand integrations with the broader AI ecosystem. While volume from AI channels is still in an early stage, adoption is building quickly. In the third quarter, page views and order volume from AI channels grew nearly 500% and 550% year over year, respectively. Notably, AI is demonstrating distinct advantages in categories such as consumer electronics and furniture, where shoppers weigh multiple options before buying. In these categories, AI can better interpret consumer needs, recommend relevant products, and guide shoppers toward a purchase. SHOPLINE Omi, an AI-powered commerce assistant, has rolled out features spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, guidance on platform features and settings, and detailed store performance analysis, bringing AI deeper into merchants' day-to-day workflows and improving operational efficiency.

MT. LAUREL, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--InTest Corporation (NYSE American: INTT), a global supplier of innovative test and process technology solutions, today announced the launch of the BT-28 ECO, a next-generation benchtop air forcing system from InTest Thermal Solutions. Designed to meet and exceed the requirements of European Union Regulation (EU) 2024/573, the BT-28 ECO advances precision thermal testing while helping customers respond to a rapidly changing refrigerant and sustainability landscape.

“We designed the BT-28 ECO to meet emerging European F-gas requirements without asking customers to give up speed, accuracy, workspace or ease of use. It is a strong example of our commitment to helping customers boost performance while preparing their operations for a more sustainable future,” said Scott Taylor, Vice President and General Manager of InTest’s Environmental Technologies division.

“The BT-28 ECO shows how InTest’s leadership and focus on innovation in precision temperature control translate into value-creating solutions for our customers,” added Rich Rogoff, President and Chief Executive Officer of InTest Corporation.

The BT-28 ECO delivers a temperature range of -28°C to +225°C utilizing refrigerants with a GWP less than 5.0. It transitions from -10°C to +125°C, and back, in approximately 10 seconds or less, while providing 14 scfm (6.5 l/s) airflow across the full temperature range. The system delivers temperature resolution of ±0.1°C and temperature accuracy of 1.0°C when calibrated against a NIST standard.

Engineered for laboratories and production environments where floor and bench space are at a premium, the portable system measures approximately 13.9 inches wide by 23.4 inches deep by 16.7 inches high and weighs approximately 80 pounds. Its ECO-Stream design is smaller, quieter and more energy-efficient, with operating sound levels below 60 dBA and below 50 dBA at idle.

BT-28 ECO Highlights

Regulatory readiness
Designed to meet and exceed EU 2024/573 requirements and support the transition to lower-GWP refrigerants.

Industry-leading benchtop performance
Fast transitions, 14 scfm airflow and a -28°C to +225°C operating range.

Compact, quiet operation
Portable benchtop footprint with <60 dBA operation and <50 dBA at idle.

Flexible control
Detachable touchscreen with a 9-foot (3-meter) remote cable and proprietary direct DUT temperature control.

Serviceability and safety
Auto-diagnostics, field-replaceable modules and operator-set high and low temperature limits.

 

The detachable touchscreen can be positioned within the reach of the supplied remote cable, giving operators greater flexibility around the test area. Available accessories include thermal caps, bench clamps, a control cradle, tall and short carts, custom enclosures and non-conductive mats.

About InTest Thermal Solutions

InTest Thermal Solutions specializes in the design and manufacture of thermal test, process cooling and biomedical cold storage systems. Its product portfolio and in-house engineering capabilities provide precision temperature control solutions for demanding environments ranging from -185°C to +500°C, with rapid transitions or long dwell times. InTest Thermal Solutions is a wholly owned subsidiary of InTest Corporation.

About InTest Corporation

InTest Corporation is a global supplier of innovative test and process technology solutions for use in manufacturing and testing across a wide range of markets, including automotive, defense/aerospace, industrial, life sciences, semiconductor and telecommunications. Backed by decades of engineering expertise and a culture of operational excellence, InTest solves difficult thermal, mechanical and electronic challenges for customers worldwide. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Prospect Prediction Markets Inc. (TSXV: MKT) (OTCQB: MKTSF) (FSE: DEP) ("Prospect Markets" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that Mr. Kevin Gopaul has been nominated for election to the Company's board of directors at its upcoming annual general meeting of shareholders (the "Meeting"), scheduled to be held on December 30, 2026.

Mr. Gopaul currently serves as a strategic advisor to the Company. If elected, he will bring nearly 30 years of experience in capital markets and asset management, including senior leadership roles in the Canadian exchange-traded fund industry.

"Kevin built one of Canada's leading ETF businesses from scratch. He knows how to launch new products, earn the trust of institutions and regulators, and hold a company to the highest governance standards. That's exactly the experience we need on our board as we scale following our U.S. launch."

"I'm pleased to be nominated for election to the board of Prospect Markets. Having worked with the team as a strategic advisor, I look forward to contributing my experience to support the Company's next phase of growth," said Kevin Gopaul.

About Mr. Gopaul

Mr. Gopaul has nearly 30 years of experience in the investment management industry, spanning research, trading, portfolio management and executive leadership. He has been Chief Executive Officer of VanEck Canada Inc. since April 2026.

Before that, he spent more than 14 years at BMO Global Asset Management, where he helped build BMO Exchange Traded Funds from its inception into one of Canada's leading ETF businesses, surpassing $100 billion in assets. His roles at BMO included Global Head of Exchange Traded Funds, CEO and Country Head for Canada, and Chief Investment Officer for Canada, overseeing investment teams in Hong Kong, London and Chicago.

Earlier in his career, Mr. Gopaul held senior roles with Barclays Global Investors, Scotia Capital and Sun Life Financial, working across both institutional and retail investor channels.

Mr. Gopaul has been an active contributor to the Canadian financial services industry. He was the founding and longest-serving director of the Canadian ETF Association (CETFA) and has served on the Public Policy Committee of the Canadian Coalition for Good Governance (CCGG).

HONG KONG, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Futu Holdings Limited (“Futu” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: FUTU), a leading tech-driven online brokerage and wealth management platform, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Operational Highlights

  • Total number of funded accounts1 increased 27.9% year-over-year to 4,005,858 as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total number of brokerage accounts2 increased 22.5% year-over-year to 6,868,829 as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total number of users3 increased 13.8% year-over-year to 32.0 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total client assets increased 7.6% year-over-year to HK$1.33 trillion as of September 30, 2026.
  • Daily average client assets were HK$1.33 trillion in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 21.1% from the same period in 2025.
  • Total trading volume in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 28.4% year-over-year to HK$5.01 trillion, in which trading volume for U.S. stocks was HK$3.81 trillion, and trading volume for Hong Kong stocks was HK$942.5 billion.
  • Margin financing and securities lending balance increased 17.1% year-over-year to HK$73.8 billion as of September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights 

  • Total revenues increased 4.5% year-over-year to HK$6,690.6 million (US$852.7 million). 
  • Total gross profit was largely stable year-over-year to HK$5,630.5 million (US$717.6 million).
  • Net income was largely stable year-over-year to HK$3,186.7 million (US$406.1 million). 
  • Non-GAAP adjusted net income⁴ was largely stable year-over-year to HK$3,272.4 million (US$417.0 million).

Mr. Leaf Hua Li, Futu’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, said, “While equity market conditions softened during the past quarter and investor sentiment became more cautious, our business remained resilient. During the quarter, we deepened our relationships with clients, broadened our multi-asset product capabilities, and continued to diversify our geographic mix and revenue base. These developments reinforce our confidence in the direction of our long-term strategy, while we remain focused on disciplined execution.”

“As of quarter-end, our total funded accounts reached 4.0 million, up 27.9% year-over-year. We added 163 thousand net new funded accounts in the quarter despite challenging equity markets and mixed news across certain regions. Excluding mainland China and Japan, net new funded accounts would have been approximately 173 thousand. International markets remain primary growth engine, with Malaysia contributing the largest number of net new funded account additions, followed by Singapore and Hong Kong, reflecting a diversified geographic profile of growth. Our average client retention rate remained above 98%, showing our ability to support clients through changing market conditions and evolving investment needs.”

“We delivered resilient net asset inflows of approximately HK$34.5 billion during the quarter despite challenging market conditions, supported by an expanding product suite and deeper customer engagement. Total client assets were HK$1.33 trillion as of quarter end, up 7.6% year-over-year and down 4.6% quarter-over-quarter. The sequential decline was primarily attributable to lower market valuations. Margin financing and securities lending balance declined 22.3% quarter-over-quarter to HK$73.8 billion, largely reflecting a high comparison base in the prior quarter, while remaining higher year-over-year.”

“Our strategic transition towards a broader wealth management platform gained traction during the quarter. Client assets in wealth management increased 11.8% year-over-year and 9.0% quarter-over-quarter to HK$196.4 billion. During the quarter, clients rotated into money market funds amid a more cautious investment sentiment. We further broadened our product offering with two Hong Kong market firsts: a weekly-dealing public mutual fund and a fully tokenized gold ETF. To meet the increasingly sophisticated trading and asset allocation needs of high-net-worth clients, we launched over-the-counter derivatives trading in Hong Kong and introduced a wholesale fund in Malaysia. Our AI assistant has also expanded into wealth management, supporting clients throughout the investment process, from portfolio analysis and fund selection to ongoing monitoring. As a result, wealth management penetration climbed to 28.2%, representing 1.13 million customers.”

“Total trading volume was HK$5.01 trillion, up 28.4% year-over-year and down 22.0% quarter-over-quarter, as softer equity market conditions, particularly a sharp pullback in semiconductor and AI-related names, dampened client trading activity. U.S. stock trading volume declined 24.0% sequentially to HK$3.81 trillion. Hong Kong stock trading volume declined 19.2% quarter-over-quarter to HK$942.5 billion.”

“Amid continued strength in Hong Kong’s IPO market, we provided IPO-related services to more than 70% of new listings and served as joint bookrunners for several prominent IPOs, including those of Momenta, Longsys, and Mech-Mind Robotics.”

“Despite near-term volatility across global equity markets, we remain confident in our long-term outlook. Rising investable wealth across Asia, growing demand for multi-asset allocation, and continued adoption of digital financial services remain long-term growth drivers. Our priorities remain clear: deepening client relationships, expanding our wealth management capabilities and strengthening our international franchise, laying the foundation for sustainable growth.”

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Total revenues were HK$6,690.6 million (US$852.7 million), an increase of 4.5% from HK$6,402.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. 

Brokerage commission and handling charge income was HK$2,793.9 million (US$356.1 million), a decrease of 4.1% from the third quarter of 2025. This was mainly due to the decrease in blended commission rate from 7.5bps to 5.6bps, partially offset by the 28.4% year-over-year increase in total trading volume.

Interest income was HK$3,161.8 million (US$403.0 million), an increase of 3.8% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was mainly driven by higher interest income from margin financing and bank deposit, largely offset by the decrease in interest income from securities borrowing and lending business. 

Other income was HK$734.8 million (US$93.6 million), an increase of 65.5% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher currency exchange income and fund distribution service income. 

Costs

Total costs were HK$1,060.0 million (US$135.1million), an increase of 33.6% compared to HK$793.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. 

Brokerage commission and handling charge expenses were HK$238.8 million (US$30.4 million), an increase of 48.7% from the third quarter of 2025. This increase was mainly driven by the growth of trading volume. 

Interest expenses were HK$585.6 million (US$74.6 million), an increase of 23.6% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher expenses associated with our margin financing.

Processing and servicing costs were HK$235.6 million (US$30.0 million), an increase of 48.0% from the third quarter of 2025. The increase was primarily due to increasing cloud service fees. 

Gross Profit

Total gross profit was HK$5,630.5 million (US$717.6 million), largely stable from HK$5,609.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Gross margin was 84.2%, as compared to 87.6% in the third quarter of 2025. 

Operating Expenses

Total operating expenses were HK$1,590.4 million (US$202.7 million), a decrease of 6.7% from HK$1,704.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. 

Research and development expenses were HK$483.9 million (US$61.7 million), a decrease of 15.7% from the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to effective cost-control measures.

Selling and marketing expenses were HK$545.1 million (US$69.5 million), a decrease of 6.9% from HK$585.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to fewer net new funded accounts in the quarter.

General and administrative expenses were HK$561.4 million (US$71.5 million), an increase of 3.0% from HK$545.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The increase was mainly driven by higher office rental expenses.

Income from Operations

Income from operations increased by 3.5% to HK$4,040.1 million (US$514.9 million) from HK$3,904.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. Operating margin was 60.4%, largely stable compared to 61.0% in the third quarter of 2025. 

Net Income

Net income was largely stable at HK$3,186.7million (US406.1 million) from HK$3,217.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Net income margin for the third quarter of 2026 declined to 47.6% from 50.2% in the year-ago quarter.

Non-GAAP adjusted net income was largely stable at HK$3,272.4 million (US$417.0 million) from the third quarter of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted net income is defined as net income excluding share-based compensation expenses. For further information, see "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" at the bottom of this press release.

Net Income per ADS

Basic net income per American Depositary Share ("ADS") was HK$23.36 (US$2.98), compared with HK$23.20 in the third quarter of 2025. Diluted net income per ADS was HK$23.20 (US$2.96), compared with HK$22.80 in the third quarter of 2025. Each ADS represents eight Class A ordinary shares.

About Futu Holdings Limited

Futu Holdings Limited (Nasdaq: FUTU) is an advanced technology company transforming the investing experience by offering fully digitalized financial services. Through its proprietary digital platforms, Futubull and Moomoo, the Company provides a full range of investment services, including trade execution and clearing, margin financing and securities lending, and wealth management. The Company has embedded social media tools to create a network centered around its users and provide connectivity to users, investors, companies, analysts, media and key opinion leaders. The Company also provides corporate services, including IPO distribution, investor relations and ESOP solution services.

Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

In evaluating the business, the Company considers and uses non-GAAP adjusted net income, a non-GAAP measure, as a supplemental measure to review and assess its operating performance. The presentation of the non-GAAP financial measure is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted net income as net income excluding share-based compensation expenses. The Company presents the non-GAAP financial measure because it is used by the management to evaluate the operating performance and formulate business plans. Non-GAAP adjusted net income enables the management to assess the Company's operating results without considering the impact of share-based compensation expenses, which are non-cash charges. The Company also believes that the use of the non-GAAP measure facilitates investors' assessment of its operating performance.

Non-GAAP adjusted net income is not defined under U.S. GAAP and is not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. This non-GAAP financial measure has limitations as analytical tools. One of the key limitations of using non-GAAP adjusted net income is that it does not reflect all items of expense that affect the Company's operations. Share-based compensation expenses have been and may continue to be incurred in the business and is not reflected in the presentation of non-GAAP adjusted net income. Further, the non-GAAP measure may differ from the non-GAAP information used by other companies, including peer companies, and therefore their comparability may be limited.

The Company compensates for these limitations by reconciling the non-GAAP financial measure to the nearest U.S. GAAP performance measure, all of which should be considered when evaluating the Company's performance.

  • Gross billings (non-GAAP) were RMB239.0 million (US$35.6 million), compared to RMB349.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross profit was RMB273.4 million (US$40.8 million), compared to RMB462.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net income was RMB35.2 million (US$5.2 million), compared to RMB125.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net income margin1 was 10.6%, compared to 24.0% in the third quarter of 2025.
  • New student enrollments2 were 84,879, compared to 137,493 in the third quarter of 2025.
  • As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s deferred revenue balance was RMB382.5 million (US$57.1 million), compared to RMB585.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

1 Net income margin is defined as net income as a percentage of net revenues.
2 New student enrollments for a given period refer to the total number of orders placed by students that newly enroll in at least one course during that period, including those students that enroll and then terminate their enrollment with us, excluding orders of our low-price courses, such as “mini courses” and “RMB1 courses”, which we offer in the form of recorded videos or short live streaming, to strengthen our competitiveness and improve customer experience.

Mr. Tongbo Liu, Chief Executive Officer of Sunlands, commented, “During the third quarter of 2026, we remained focused on our core business, refining our course offerings and teaching services to better address evolving learner needs. As demand for lifelong learning among middle-aged and senior learners continues to diversify, we are placing greater emphasis on course quality, personalized learning experiences, and long-term learner engagement. Looking ahead, we will continue to build on our experience in adult education, further integrate technology into teaching and services, and strengthen our core business to support sustainable development.”

Mr. Hangyu Li, Finance Director of Sunlands, added, “In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues were RMB331.6 million and net income was RMB35.2 million, representing net income margin of 10.6%. Against a lower revenue base, we reduced operating expenses by 25.3% year-over-year and remained profitable for the 22nd consecutive quarter. We remain focused on aligning costs and resource allocation with our operating needs, preserving liquidity, and allocating capital prudently to support our core business and long-term development.”

Financial Results for the Third Quarter of 2026

Net Revenues

In the third quarter of 2026, net revenues decreased by 36.6% to RMB331.6 million (US$49.5 million) from RMB523.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the year-over-year decline in gross billings.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues decreased by 3.6% to RMB58.1 million (US$8.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB60.3 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined service fees paid to educational institutions.

Gross Profit

Gross profit decreased by 40.9% to RMB273.4 million (US$40.8 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB462.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Operating Expenses

In the third quarter of 2026, operating expenses were RMB242.2 million (US$36.1 million), representing a 25.3% decrease from RMB324.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 26.4% to RMB206.0 million (US$30.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB279.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the decreases of compensation for sales personnel and the spending on branding and marketing activities focused on interest courses offerings.

General and administrative expenses decreased by 18.7% to RMB29.2 million (US$4.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB36.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Product development expenses decreased by 18.9% to RMB7.0 million (US$1.0 million) in the third quarter of 2026 from RMB8.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined compensation expenses related to the Company’s product development personnel.

Net Income

Net income for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB35.2 million (US$5.2 million), as compared to RMB125.4 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share

Basic and diluted net income per share was RMB5.53 (US$0.83) in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to RMB18.64 in the third quarter of 2025.

Cash, Cash Equivalents, Restricted Cash and Short-term Investments

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had RMB502.0 million (US$74.9 million) of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash and RMB281.4 million (US$42.0 million) of short-term investments, as compared to RMB576.8 million of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash and RMB235.9 million of short-term investments as of December 31, 2025.

Deferred Revenue

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a deferred revenue balance of RMB382.5 million (US$57.1 million), as compared to RMB585.3 million as of December 31, 2025.

Share Repurchase

On May 29, 2026, the Company’s board of directors authorized a share repurchase program, under which the Company may repurchase up to US$50.0 million of Class A ordinary shares in the form of ADSs over the next 36 months. As of November 17, 2026, the Company had repurchased an aggregate of 716,479 ADSs for approximately US$2.4 million under the share repurchase program.

Financial Results for the First Nine Months of 2026

Net Revenues

In the first nine months of 2026, net revenues decreased by 23.9% to RMB1,178.6 million (US$175.8 million) from RMB1,549.7 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the year-over-year decline in gross billings.

Cost of Revenues

Cost of revenues decreased by 13.6% to RMB174.9 million (US$26.1 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB202.3 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to declined cost of revenues from sales of goods such as learning materials and books and decreased service fees paid to educational institutions.

Gross Profit

Gross profit decreased by 25.5% to RMB1,003.7 million (US$149.7 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB1,347.4 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Operating Expenses

In the first nine months of 2026, operating expenses were RMB792.2 million (US$118.2 million), representing a 21.4% decrease from RMB1,008.1 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 23.4% to RMB676.2 million (US$100.9 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB882.7 million in the first nine months of 2025. The decrease was mainly due to the decreases of compensation for sales personnel and the spending on branding and marketing activities focused on interest courses offerings.

General and administrative expenses decreased by 6.4% to RMB96.9 million (US$14.5 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB103.6 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Product development expenses decreased by 12.5% to RMB19.1 million (US$2.9 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RMB21.9 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Net Income

Net income for the first nine months of 2026 was RMB195.5 million (US$29.2 million), compared with RMB327.3 million in the first nine months of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income Per Share

Basic and diluted net income per share was RMB29.79 (US$4.44) in the first nine months of 2026, compared with RMB48.50 in the first nine months of 2025.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Sunlands currently expects net revenues to be between RMB220 million to RMB240 million, which would represent a decrease of between 49.0% to 53.2% year-over-year. The above outlook is based on the current market conditions and reflects the Company’s current and preliminary estimates of market and operating conditions and customer demand, which are all subject to substantial uncertainty.

Exchange Rate

The Company’s business is primarily conducted in China and all revenues are denominated in Renminbi (“RMB”). This announcement contains currency conversions of RMB amounts into U.S. dollars (“US$”) solely for the convenience of the reader. Unless otherwise noted, all translations from RMB to US$ are made at a rate of RMB6.7045 to US$1.00, the effective noon buying rate for September 30, 2026 as set forth in the H.10 statistical release of the Federal Reserve Board. No representation is made that the RMB amounts could have been, or could be, converted, realized or settled into US$ at that rate on September 30, 2026, or at any other rate.

About Sunlands

Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE: STG) (“Sunlands” or the “Company”), formerly known as Sunlands Online Education Group, is a leader in China’s adult online education market and China’s adult personal interest learning market. With a one to many live streaming platform, Sunlands offers various degree- or diploma-oriented post-secondary courses as well as professional certification preparation, professional skills and interest courses. Students can access the Company's services either through PC or mobile applications. The Company's online platform cultivates a personalized, interactive learning environment by featuring a virtual learning community and a vast library of educational content offerings that adapt to the learning habits of its students. Sunlands offers a unique approach to education research and development that organizes subject content into Learning Outcome Trees, the Company's proprietary knowledge management system. Sunlands has a deep understanding of the educational needs of its prospective students and offers solutions that help them achieve their goals.

About Non-GAAP Financial Measures

We use gross billings, EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP operating cost and expenses, non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP net income per share, each a non-GAAP financial measure, in evaluating our operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes.

We define gross billings for a specific period as the total amount of cash received for the sale of course packages, net of the total amount of refunds paid in such period. Our management uses gross billings as a performance measurement because we generally bill our students for the entire course tuition at the time of sale of our course packages and recognize revenue proportionally over a period. EBITDA is defined as net income excluding depreciation and amortization, interest expense, interest income, and income tax expenses. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income excluding depreciation and amortization, interest expense, interest income, income tax expenses and impairment loss on long-lived assets. We believe that gross billings, EBITDA and adjusted EBITDA provide valuable insight into the sales of our course packages and the performance of our business.

These non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered in isolation from, or as a substitute for, their most directly comparable financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP. SHANGHAI, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ATRenew Inc. ("ATRenew" or the "Company") (NYSE: RERE), a pioneer in technology-driven recycling and trade-in solutions for consumer products in China, today announced its unaudited financial results for the three months ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Highlights

  • Total net revenues grew by 25.3% to RMB6,452.9 million (US$962.5 million) from RMB5,149.2 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Income from operations increased by 57.9% to RMB190.7 million (US$28.5 million) from RMB120.8 million in the same period of 2025. Adjusted income from operations (non-GAAP)1 grew by 50.7% to RMB211.5 million (US$31.5 million) from RMB140.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Net income increased by 53.6% to RMB139.5 million (US$20.8 million) from RMB90.8 million in the same period of 2025. Adjusted net income (non-GAAP)1 grew by 45.3% to RMB160.1 million (US$23.9 million) from RMB110.2 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Number of consumer products transacted2 was 12.0 million compared to 10.9 million in the same period of 2025.

Mr. Kerry Xuefeng Chen, Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer of ATRenew, commented, "We are pleased to announce that ATRenew has once again delivered solid growth in the third quarter of 2026, with total net revenues reaching RMB6,452.9 million, up 25.3% year-over-year. We have continued to refine our supply chain capabilities for pre-owned mobile phones and digital products, leveraging our industry-leading collection and fulfillment infrastructure to aggregate quality supply. By adhering to rigorous standards for refurbishment and preparation, we continue to advance quality standards in the pre-owned sector, offering users high-value, high-quality products. On the platform side, we have continued to execute our strategy of extending services to a broader base of small and medium-sized merchants, while enhancing the user experience and expanding the range of scenarios for our multi-category recycling business." 

Mr. Rex Chen, Chief Financial Officer of ATRenew, added, "In the third quarter of 2026, ATRenew's profitability continued to improve, with income from operations rising 57.9% year-over-year to RMB190.7 million and adjusted income from operations (non-GAAP) rising 50.7% year-over-year to RMB211.5 million. We also saw a year-over-year improvement in fulfillment and sales and marketing spending efficiency—a positive outcome driven by our focus on refined operations and economies of scale. Furthermore, we have actively pursued share repurchases, totaling approximately US$6.6 million in the third quarter, bringing the cumulative value of repurchases for the first nine months of 2026 to approximately US$13.5 million. Moving forward, we remain committed to scaling our business and enhancing operational efficiency, while continuing to create long-term value for both our users and our shareholders."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

REVENUE

Total net revenues increased by 25.3% to RMB6,452.9 million (US$962.5 million) from RMB5,149.2 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Net product revenues increased by 27.0% to RMB6,004.2 million (US$895.6 million) from RMB4,726.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to an increase in the sales of pre-owned consumer electronics through the Company's online channels.
  • Net service revenues increased by 6.1% to RMB448.7 million (US$66.9 million), compared to RMB422.8 million in the same period of 2025. This increase was primarily due to an increase in the service revenue generated from multi-category recycling business and PJT Marketplace.

OPERATING COSTS AND EXPENSES

Operating costs and expenses were RMB6,263.5 million (US$934.2 million), compared to RMB5,033.2 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 24.4%.

  • Merchandise costs were RMB5,140.1 million (US$766.7 million), compared to RMB4,094.2 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 25.5%. The increase was primarily due to the growth in product sales.
  • Fulfillment expenses were RMB510.4 million (US$76.1 million), compared to RMB437.1 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 16.8%. The increase was primarily due to (i) an increase in personnel costs driven by the growth of the Company's business, and (ii) an increase in operating center related expenses as the Company conducted more recycling and transaction activities compared with the same period of 2025.
  • Selling and marketing expenses were RMB449.3 million (US$67.0 million), compared to RMB363.9 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 23.5%. The increase was primarily due to (i) an increase in commission expenses in relation to channel service fees, and (ii) an increase in advertising expense.
  • General and administrative expenses were RMB94.5 million (US$14.1 million), compared to RMB74.1 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 27.5%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in personnel costs, sales tax and associated charges, and share-based compensation expenses.
  • Research and development expenses were RMB69.1 million (US$10.3 million), compared to RMB63.8 million in the same period of 2025, representing an increase of 8.3%. The increase was primarily due to an increase in personnel costs.

INCOME FROM OPERATIONS

Income from operations was RMB190.7 million (US$28.5 million), representing an increase of 57.9% from RMB120.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Adjusted income from operations (non-GAAP) was RMB211.5 million (US$31.5 million), representing an increase of 50.7% from RMB140.3 million in the same period of 2025.

NET INCOME

Net income was RMB139.5 million (US$20.8 million), representing an increase of 53.6% from RMB90.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Adjusted net income (non-GAAP) was RMB160.1 million (US$23.9 million), representing an increase of 45.3% from RMB110.2 million in the same period of 2025.

BASIC AND DILUTED NET INCOME PER ORDINARY SHARE

Basic and diluted net income per ordinary share were RMB0.87 (US$0.13) and RMB0.87 (US$0.13), compared to RMB0.56 and RMB0.56 in the same period of 2025.

Adjusted basic and diluted net income per ordinary share (non-GAAP) were RMB1.00 (US$0.15) and RMB0.99 (US$0.15), compared to RMB0.68 and RMB0.68 in the same period of 2025.

CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS, RESTRICTED CASH, SHORT-TERM INVESTMENTS AND FUNDS RECEIVABLE FROM THIRD PARTY PAYMENT SERVICE PROVIDERS

Cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term investments and funds receivable from third party payment service providers were RMB1,941.5 million (US$289.6 million) as of September 30, 2026, as compared to RMB2,187.4 million as of December 31, 2025.

Business Outlook

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Company currently expects its total revenues to be between RMB7,780.0 million and RMB7,880.0 million, representing an increase of 24.4% to 26.0% year-over-year. This forecast only reflects the Company's current and preliminary views on the market and operational conditions, which are subject to change.

On June 30, 2025, the board of directors of the Company (the "Board") authorized a new share repurchase program, under which the Company may repurchase up to US$50 million of its shares (including ADSs) over a 12-month period starting from June 30, 2025. On May 19, 2026, the Board authorized an extension of the existing share repurchase program for an additional 12-month period commencing from June 30, 2026, with other key terms remaining unchanged. During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased a total of approximately 1.6 million ADSs for approximately US$6.6 million. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The Company also uses certain non-GAAP financial measures in evaluating its business. For example, the Company uses adjusted income from operations, adjusted net income and adjusted net income per ordinary share as supplemental measures to review and assess its financial and operating performance. The presentation of these non-GAAP financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation, or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. Adjusted income from operations is income from operations excluding the share-based compensation expenses and amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions. Adjusted net income is net income excluding the share-based compensation expenses and amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions and tax effects of amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions. Adjusted net income per ordinary share is adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by weighted average number of shares used in calculating net income per ordinary share.

The Company presents non-GAAP financial measures because they are used by the Company's management to evaluate the Company's financial and operating performance and formulate business plans. The Company believes that adjusted income from operations and adjusted net income help identify underlying trends in the Company's business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that are included in income from operations and net income. The Company also believes that the use of non-GAAP financial measures facilitates investors' assessment of the Company's operating performance. The Company believes that adjusted income from operations and adjusted net income provide useful information about the Company's operating results, enhance the overall understanding of the Company's past performance and future prospects and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by the Company's management in its financial and operational decision making.

The non-GAAP financial measures are not defined under U.S. GAAP and are not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools. One of the key limitations of using non-GAAP financial measures is that they do not reflect all items of income and expense that affect the Company's operations. The share-based compensation expenses, amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions and tax effects of amortization of intangible assets resulting from assets and business acquisitions have been and may continue to be incurred in the Company's business and are not reflected in the presentation of non-GAAP financial measures. Further, the non-GAAP measures may differ from the non-GAAP measures used by other companies, including peer companies, potentially limiting the comparability of their financial results to the Company's. In light of the foregoing limitations, the non-GAAP financial measures for the period should not be considered in isolation from or as an alternative to income from operations, net income, and net income attributable to ordinary shareholders per share, or other financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

BETHESDA, Md.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Walker & Dunlop, Inc. announced today that it has arranged $270,000,000 in refinancing for The Greyson, a 28-story, 622-unit, Class A mixed-use residential tower developed by Nasser Freres in the heart of Jersey City's Journal Square neighborhood. The financing marks a significant milestone for the development, supporting its transition from construction to stabilized operations and positioning the property for long-term success.

The Greyson. Photo credits: Nasser Freres

Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory served as exclusive advisor to Nasser Freres, arranging a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan from affiliates of Apollo. The transaction was arranged by Keith Kurland, Aaron Appel, Adam Schwartz, Jonathan Schwartz, Jordan Casella, Christopher de Raet, and Jack Krentzman.

"Journal Square has undergone a remarkable transformation, and The Greyson exemplifies the caliber of development attracting investment to the neighborhood,” said Kurland, senior managing director of Capital Markets and co-head of Institutional Advisory at Walker & Dunlop. "With its exceptional location, extensive amenities, and proximity to Manhattan, the property is well-positioned to capitalize on the area’s continued growth. We’re pleased to have worked with Nasser Freres and Apollo to execute this transaction.”

Located at 25 Cottage Street, The Greyson encompasses 424,328 rentable square feet, including 389,328 square feet of residential and 35,000 square feet of commercial space. The property features a collection of studio, one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences with unobstructed views of the Jersey City skyline. Designed to deliver an elevated residential experience, The Greyson offers an extensive suite of amenities, including an art gallery, children's playroom, screening room, gaming lounge, virtual reality and sports room, coffee bar, fitness center, speakeasy, and private event space. Ground-floor retail space leased to a wine bar further enhances the property’s appeal while contributing to Journal Square’s growing dining and entertainment scene.

"From the outset, our vision for The Greyson was to create something truly distinctive, a property that would help shape the next chapter of residential living in Journal Square while contributing meaningfully to the neighborhood’s continued transformation,” said Michael Sokoloff, partner at Nasser Freres. "We’ve been intentional about every aspect of this development, from its architecture and design to the amenities and experiences we’re bringing to residents. We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve built and believe The Greyson will set a new standard for the neighborhood for years to come. This refinancing marks an exciting next chapter as we shift our focus to the property’s long-term success and we appreciate Walker & Dunlop’s advisory.”

Situated along the newly opened Homestead commercial corridor, the property is less than a five-minute walk from the Journal Square Transportation Center, offering direct PATH access to Lower and Midtown Manhattan in approximately 10 and 20 minutes, respectively. Journal Square has emerged as one of the New York metropolitan area's fastest-growing rental submarkets, driven by demand for transit-oriented housing and rental rates that remain comparatively affordable to those along the Jersey City Waterfront and in Manhattan.

In the first half of 2026, Walker & Dunlop’s Capital Markets team sourced over $13.9 billion from non-Agency capital providers, including nearly $9.6 billion for multifamily properties. This vast experience has made them a top advisor on all asset classes for many of the industry’s top developers, owners, and operators. To learn more about Walker & Dunlop’s broad financing options, visit our website.

Walker & Dunlop (NYSE: WD) is one of the largest commercial real estate finance and advisory services firms in the United States and internationally. Our ideas and capital create communities where people live, work, shop, and play. Our innovative people, breadth of our brand, and our technological capabilities make us one of the most insightful and client-focused firms in the commercial real estate industry.

Key Terms

floating-ratefinancial
A floating-rate is an interest rate on a loan, bond or other debt that moves up or down over time based on a regularly published reference number, so the payments change as market rates change. For investors, that means income and interest costs track current market conditions—like a thermostat that adjusts with room temperature—offering protection when rates rise but adding uncertainty about future cash flow.
interest-onlyfinancial
A loan or payment plan where the borrower pays only the interest for a set period while the original loan amount (the principal) stays unchanged; after that period payments typically rise to cover principal or a lump-sum principal payment is due. For investors this matters because interest-only structures change cash flows and risk: they can boost short-term income but increase the chance of payment shock or default later, similar to renting a car without paying down the purchase cost until the final bill arrives.
bridge loanfinancial
A bridge loan is a short-term loan used to quickly provide funds until a larger, long-term financing option is in place. It acts like a temporary bridge, helping individuals or businesses cover immediate expenses or complete transactions without delay. TORONTO, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Talisker Resources Ltd. ("Talisker" or the "Company") (TSX: TSK, OTCQX: TSKFF) is pleased to provide an update on the continued advancement of its ore sorter facility (“Sorting Facility”) at the Company’s 100% owned Bralorne Gold Project (“Bralorne”).   Construction and engineering activities have continued to advance according to plan, with several major project milestones already completed and a number of critical work programs now entering the execution phase.

Key Highlights:

  • Initial operation of the Sorting Facility is targeted for Q2 2027, with full commissioning expected in July-August 2027.
  • Electrical infrastructure is completed and targeted for commissioning by the end of November 2026, providing power for the future operation of the Sorting Facility.
  • Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorting Facility were successfully completed in September.
  • Phase 2 earthworks and concrete foundation construction is planned to commence late November 2026, following removal of legacy infrastructure.
  • Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) of the TOMRA XRT Sorter is scheduled for early December 2026, with the ore sorter expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.
  • Major long-lead equipment procurement is substantially complete, with the jaw crusher, cone crusher, vibrating screen plant received in Bralorne in October, conveyors, compressors, and buildings being delivered in phases starting December 2026.
  • Construction and mechanical installation activities are planned throughout Q1 2027, supported by completion of detailed engineering and issuance of the remaining construction tender packages in December 2026.

Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorter Facility was successfully completed in September. The electrical infrastructure has been procured and installed, with final commissioning scheduled for the end of November 2026. The Mustang Mine power generation and distribution system consists of two 1.5 MW diesel generators, providing a total installed generation capacity of 3 MW at 600 V. The generators can operate in parallel or independently, providing redundancy and backup capability.

Power for the underground mining operations is stepped up to 4.16 kV through a 3,200 kVA transformer and distributed to underground substations that will supply mining equipment.

Surface power distribution is installed and ready to serve the sorting and crushing facilities, as well as supporting all other surface infrastructure requirements. The electrical system incorporates protective switchgear, circuit breakers, ground-fault monitoring, and neutral grounding resistors to ensure safe and reliable operation during the next phase of project development. The power plant and distribution network have also been designed to accommodate the future addition of a third generator unit, allowing for straightforward expansion of site power capacity as operational requirements increase.

As part of the ore sorter site preparation activities, a legacy electrical system located within the planned Sorting Facility footprint has been safely dismantled and removed, clearing part of the area for Phase 2 Earthworks construction. In parallel, the Company has completed construction of a new tension-fabric steel frame heavy-duty mechanic shop and is currently transitioning operations from the legacy shop. Demolition of the former shop is expected to be completed in November, fully opening the sorter site for Phase 2 Earthworks before the end of November.

The Phase 2 Earthworks and concrete contractor is scheduled to mobilize to site in November, marking the beginning of a major construction phase. This work will include cut-and-fill activities, foundation preparation, and pre-cast concrete installation within the area previously occupied by the legacy electrical infrastructure and mechanic shop.

Detailed engineering for the project continues to progress well. Issue-for-Tender packages covering the remaining construction components including equipment installation, electrical and mechanical are expected to be completed in December 2026, positioning the project for construction execution through the first half of 2027.

Procurement efforts have been highly successful, with all major equipment purchased. Equipment is either in manufacturing or pending delivery. A proactive approach to early procurement has significantly de-risked the project schedule and supports the Company's objective of maintaining construction momentum throughout the coming months.

A key milestone will occur during the second week of December when the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) is conducted for the TOMRA XRT sorter. Following successful testing, the ore sorter is expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.

The crushing circuit has also reached an important milestone, with all major crushing equipment including the jaw crusher, cone crusher, and vibrating screen plant, now delivered and in Bralorne. The compressor system required to support sorter operations is expected to ship for delivery in January 2027.

Building fabrication remains on track, with the manufacturing of two tension-fabric steel frame buildings completed and ready for shipment. The remaining two buildings are expected to be completed and shipped in January 2027.

Engineering and fabrication of the conveyor systems is progressing well. Initial conveyor deliveries are expected to begin arriving on site in mid-December, with additional conveyors being manufactured and shipped in priority sequence throughout the first quarter of 2027.

Taken together, these achievements represent substantial progress toward delivery of one of the Company's most important infrastructure projects. The project continues to transition from planning into full-scale execution with detailed engineering, procurement, and construction activities advancing simultaneously.

The Sorting Facility remains on schedule for operational readiness in the second quarter of 2027, with full commissioning anticipated during July-August 2027. Pre-commissioning activities will involve sorting existing stockpile inventory, providing an opportunity to validate system performance ahead of full scale operations. Once operational, the Sorting Facility will process run-of-mine material and is expected to enhance gold grades while eliminating dilution prior to trucking and shipping, improve operating efficiencies, reduce transportation costs, and strengthen project economics.

Terry Harbort, President and CEO, stated, "We are very pleased with the progress being made on the Sorting Facility. With key infrastructure completed, major equipment secured, and construction activities continuing to ramp up, the project remains on schedule for operational readiness in Q2 2027. This Sorting Facility represents an important milestone for Bralorne and will play a significant role in improving operational efficiency and supporting the Company's long-term growth objectives."


Figure 1: Aerial view of the Mustang Mine site with a rendered overlay of the sorting facility. The recently completed machine shop and the Mustang Mine power generation systems are shown to scale in their actual locations. The Sorting Facility rendering is provided for conceptual illustration only and may not be to scale. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence from 1 through 4.


Figure 2: 3D rendering of the Sorting Facility. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence. Run-of-mine material is loaded into the jaw crusher (1) via the loading ramp and conveyed to the triple-deck screening plant (2). Screened material is then transported to the TOMRA XRT sorter (3), where gold-bearing material is separated from waste rock. The sorted product is conveyed to the cone crusher (4) before being stockpiled within a covered tension-fabric storage building. Waste reject material is conveyed to a separate waste stockpile.
